# libtmux-lisp [![Native Lisp checks](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-lisp/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-lisp/actions/workflows/tests.yml) [![libtmux.org](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-libtmux.org-0b7285)](https://libtmux.org/en/lisp/) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-lisp/blob/master/LICENSE)
Drive tmux from Common Lisp: [sessions][api-session], [windows][api-window], [window links][api-window-link] and [panes][api-pane] as CLOS objects, queried with plain sequences, changed through an explicit [`client`][api-client]. [Documentation](https://libtmux.org/en/lisp/) · [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/lisp/latest/reference/) · [REPL tutorial](docs/tutorial.md) **Contents** — [Install](#install-from-source) · [Start a server](#start-a-private-server) · [Drive a pane](#drive-a-pane) · [Find things](#find-sessions-windows-and-panes) · [Query](#query-a-snapshot) · [Workspaces](#build-a-workspace) · [Control](#stream-pane-output) · [Systems](#choose-an-asdf-system) · [Status](#support-and-status) · [Guides](#find-the-right-guide) ## Install from source Needs SBCL, Linux (WSL included) and tmux 3.3a or newer. Not released yet: load it from a checkout. ```console $ git clone https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-lisp.git && cd libtmux-lisp ``` Register the checkout with ASDF, from its root: ```lisp (asdf:load-asd (truename "libtmux.asd")) ``` Load core and queries. Both need only ASDF/UIOP: ```lisp (asdf:load-system "libtmux/query") ``` To run the examples, set up the toolchain with [mise](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md), then: ```console $ mise run examples ``` The examples run on a private tmux socket, never your default server. ## Start a private server ### [`libtmux:with-daemon`][api-with-daemon]: a server that cleans up after itself [`with-client`][api-with-client] scopes the connection; [`new-session`][api-new-session] creates a session. ```lisp (defun inspect-owned-workspace (&key (program "tmux")) "Start an isolated daemon; return owned pane data after closing both resources." (libtmux:with-daemon (daemon :program program) (libtmux:with-client (client :program (libtmux:daemon-program daemon) :socket-path (libtmux:daemon-socket-path daemon)) (let ((outcome (libtmux:new-session client :name "demo" :command '("/bin/cat")))) (when (libtmux:outcome-observation-error outcome) (error (libtmux:outcome-observation-error outcome)))) (map 'list #'libtmux:entity-data (libtmux:panes (libtmux:fetch-snapshot client)))))) ``` ```console $ mise exec -- tools/lisp.sh examples/managed-daemon.lisp ``` Prints `MANAGED DAEMON PASS` and a pane record. To reach an existing server, use `with-client` alone. More: [daemon scopes](docs/daemons.md). ## Drive a pane ### [`libtmux:split-pane`][api-split-pane]: split, send, capture and resize [`send-text`][api-send-text] types into the new pane and [`capture-pane`][api-capture-pane] reads its screen. [`resize-window`][api-resize-window] and [`resize-pane`][api-resize-pane] set sizes in cells. ```lisp (asdf:load-system "libtmux") (defun drive-panes (&key (program "tmux")) "Split a pane, send it text, capture its screen and resize; return what tmux reports." (libtmux:with-daemon (daemon :program program) (libtmux:with-client (client :program (libtmux:daemon-program daemon) :socket-path (libtmux:daemon-socket-path daemon)) (flet ((observed (outcome) (when (libtmux:outcome-observation-error outcome) (error (libtmux:outcome-observation-error outcome))) (values (libtmux:outcome-value outcome)))) (observed (libtmux:new-session client :name "demo" :command '("/bin/cat"))) (let* ((left (aref (libtmux:fetch-panes client) 0)) (right (observed (libtmux:split-pane client left :direction :horizontal :command '("/bin/cat"))))) (libtmux:send-text client right "hello from Lisp" :enter t) (let* ((text (libtmux:capture-pane client right)) (window (observed (libtmux:resize-window client (libtmux:window right) :width 100 :height 30))) (narrow (observed (libtmux:resize-pane client right :width 20)))) (list :text (string-right-trim '(#\Newline) text) :window-size (list (libtmux:width window) (libtmux:height window)) :pane-width (libtmux:width narrow)))))))) ``` ```console $ mise exec -- tools/lisp.sh examples/drive-panes.lisp ``` Prints `PANE OPERATIONS PASS`, the captured text, the window size and the pane width. A send succeeds when tmux accepts the input, not when the application reads it: [wait on a signal](docs/tutorial.md#drive-an-application-without-polling). - [`kill-pane`][api-kill-pane], [`kill-window`][api-kill-window], [`kill-session`][api-kill-session] and [`kill-server`][api-kill-server] remove targets. - [`set-option`][api-set-option] and [`set-hook`][api-set-hook] write; [`show-options`][api-show-options] and [`show-hooks`][api-show-hooks] read. More: [operation contracts](docs/operations.md) · [decoded configuration](docs/configuration.md) ## Find sessions, windows and panes ### [`libtmux:fetch-snapshot`][api-fetch-snapshot]: read the graph once One call to tmux; everything after is local. The examples share one package: `tm` is `libtmux`, `q` is `libtmux.query`, `j` is `libtmux.json` and `ws` is `libtmux.workspace`. ```lisp (defpackage #:libtmux.examples (:use #:cl) (:local-nicknames (#:tm #:libtmux) (#:q #:libtmux.query) (#:j #:libtmux.json) (#:ws #:libtmux.workspace)) (:export #:inspect-workspace #:create-workspace #:observed-value #:apply-workspace-document #:workspace-description #:terminate-owned-server #:configuration-report)) (in-package #:libtmux.examples) ``` ```lisp (defun inspect-workspace (socket-path &key (program "tmux")) "Acquire one graph from SOCKET-PATH; return owned session/window/pane data." (tm:with-client (client :program program :socket-path socket-path) (let ((snapshot (tm:fetch-snapshot client))) (loop for session across (tm:sessions snapshot) collect (list :session (tm:name session) :windows (loop for link across (tm:window-links session) for window = (tm:window link) collect (list :index (tm:index link) :name (tm:name window) :panes (map 'list #'tm:entity-data (tm:panes window))))))))) ``` A window can be linked into several sessions: ```mermaid graph LR work[Session: work] --> a[Window link: index 0] work --> b[Window link: logs] review[Session: review] --> c[Window link: index 7] review --> d[Window link: notes] a --> editor[Physical window: editor] c --> editor editor --> p1[Pane 1] editor --> p2[Pane 2] b --> logs[Physical window: logs] d --> notes[Physical window: notes] ``` More: [identity and ownership](docs/captures.md) · [walkthrough](docs/tutorial.md#build-a-linked-workspace). ### [`libtmux:panes`][api-panes]: filter with plain Lisp ```lisp (defun wide-active-panes (snapshot) "Select captured active panes at least 40 cells wide; no tmux commands." (loop for pane across (tm:panes snapshot) when (and (tm:active-p pane) (>= (tm:width pane) 40)) collect (tm:entity-data pane))) ``` ## Query a snapshot Same package nicknames as above. ### [`libtmux.query:compile-filter`][api-compile-filter]: a filter compiled once [`matching`][api-matching] applies it to captured objects. No tmux calls. ```lisp (defparameter *wide-active-filter* (q:compile-filter :pane '(:and (:= :pane/active t) (:>= :pane/width 40)))) (defun wide-active-pane-data (snapshot) "Return owned data for captured active panes at least 40 cells wide; no I/O." (map 'vector #'tm:entity-data (q:matching *wide-active-filter* (tm:panes snapshot)))) ``` Mistyped fields are refused at compile time. More: [query guide](docs/queries.md). ### [`libtmux.query:where`][api-where]: follow relations Sessions with an active pane, through window links and windows. [`items`][api-items] returns the matches. ```lisp (defparameter *active-session-filter* (q:compile-filter :session '(:any :session/window-links (:is :link/window (:any :window/panes (:= :pane/active t)))))) (defun active-session-data (snapshot) "Return owned data for sessions with an active pane; no I/O." (map 'vector #'tm:entity-data (q:items (q:where (q:from (tm:sessions snapshot) :model :session) *active-session-filter*)))) ``` ### [`libtmux.query:explain`][api-explain]: where a filter runs Lists the fields a compiled filter reads. Filters always run locally; tmux filters nothing for you. ```lisp (defun filter-execution (filter) "Report that FILTER runs locally and acquires nothing, with the fields it reads." (let ((report (q:explain filter))) (list :execution (getf report :execution) :acquires-p (getf report :acquires-p) :fields (getf report :required-fields)))) ``` For the filter above it returns: ```text (:EXECUTION :LOCAL :ACQUIRES-P NIL :FIELDS #(:PANE/ACTIVE :PANE/WIDTH)) ``` More: [inspecting a filter](docs/queries.md#inspect-owned-query-data) ### [`libtmux.json:write-filter`][api-write-filter]: regex and JSON documents Optional systems add CL-PPCRE matching and a versioned JSON form. [`read-filter`][api-read-filter] restores a filter. ```lisp (defparameter *cat-command-filter* (q:compile-filter :pane '(:regex-full-match :pane/current-command (:cl-ppcre "CAT" :case-insensitive-mode t)))) (defun cat-pane-data (snapshot) "Return owned data for captured panes whose command is exactly cat; no I/O." (map 'vector #'tm:entity-data (q:matching *cat-command-filter* (tm:panes snapshot)))) ``` ```lisp (defun round-trip-filter-document (snapshot) "Round-trip the checked regex filter and apply it to one retained snapshot." (let* ((document (j:write-filter *cat-command-filter*)) (restored (j:read-filter document :allow-regex t))) (values document (map 'vector #'tm:entity-data (q:matching restored (tm:panes snapshot)))))) ``` More: [query interchange](docs/query-interchange.md). ## Build a workspace ### [`libtmux.workspace:make-workspace`][api-make-workspace]: declare windows and panes Plain Lisp data, or an equivalent [JSON file](examples/owned-workspace.json). Nothing touches tmux until you apply it. ```lisp (defun owned-description () "Describe two windows and three panes without contacting tmux." (libtmux.workspace:make-workspace '(:schema "libtmux.lisp.workspace/2" :id "demo-workspace" :session (:id "main" :name "owned-demo" :environment #(("DEMO_LABEL" . "hello from Common Lisp")) :windows #((:id "code" :name "code" :index 2 :layout :tiled :panes #((:id "shell" :command #("/bin/cat")) (:id "repl" :command #("/bin/cat")))) (:id "logs" :name "logs" :index 5 :panes #((:id "tail" :command #("/bin/cat"))))))))) ``` ```console $ mise exec -- tools/lisp.sh examples/owned-workspace.lisp ``` ### [`libtmux.workspace:plan-workspace`][api-plan-workspace]: preview, then apply [`fetch-workspace-state`][api-fetch-workspace-state] reads tmux. The plan is local. [`apply-workspace`][api-apply-workspace] changes tmux through the client you pass. ```lisp (asdf:load-system "libtmux/workspace") (defpackage #:libtmux.workspace.example (:use #:cl) (:local-nicknames (#:tm #:libtmux) (#:ws #:libtmux.workspace))) (in-package #:libtmux.workspace.example) ``` ```lisp (defun apply-owned-description (client workspace) "Acquire, preview and apply explicitly; return the result and its owned record." (let* ((state (ws:fetch-workspace-state client workspace)) (preview (ws:plan-workspace workspace state))) (assert (getf (ws:plan-data preview) :publish-p)) (let ((result (ws:apply-workspace client workspace :total-timeout 30))) (assert (eq :succeeded (getf (ws:result-data result) :publication-status))) (values result (getf (ws:result-data result) :record))))) ``` - Changing an existing workspace needs `:reconcile t`. - A preview grants no authority to apply. More: [owned workspaces](docs/workspace-owned.md) · [Workspace API][api-workspace] · [legacy schema](docs/workspaces.md). ## Stream pane output ### [`libtmux.control:with-connection`][api-with-connection]: one connection, queued commands Needs tmux 3.8 or newer. [`submit-command`][api-submit-command] queues a request, [`await-request`][api-await-request] waits for its reply and [`next-event`][api-next-event] reads pane output as bytes. ```lisp (asdf:load-system "libtmux/control") (defpackage #:libtmux.control.example (:use #:cl) (:local-nicknames (#:tm #:libtmux) (#:control #:libtmux.control))) (in-package #:libtmux.control.example) ``` ```lisp (defun echo-through-control (client session pane) "Send literal text and collect pane-output bytes on one scoped connection." (control:with-connection (connection client session) (let ((write (control:submit-command connection (list "send-keys" "-t" (tm:id pane) "-l" "hello from control") :effect :mutation)) (enter (control:submit-command connection (list "send-keys" "-t" (tm:id pane) "Enter") :effect :mutation))) (dolist (request (list write enter)) (multiple-value-bind (result delivery) (control:await-request request :timeout 1) (assert (eq :ready delivery)) (assert (eq :completed (getf result :status)))))) (let ((bytes (make-array 0 :element-type '(unsigned-byte 8) :adjustable t :fill-pointer 0)) (expected (map 'vector #'char-code "hello from control")) (deadline (+ (get-internal-real-time) internal-time-units-per-second))) (loop repeat 64 until (search expected bytes) for remaining = (/ (- deadline (get-internal-real-time)) internal-time-units-per-second) do (assert (plusp remaining)) (multiple-value-bind (event delivery) (control:next-event connection :timeout remaining) (assert (eq :ready delivery)) (case (getf event :kind) (:output (assert (string= (tm:id pane) (getf event :pane))) (loop for byte across (getf event :data) do (vector-push-extend byte bytes))) ((:gap :end) (error "Output stream ended or lost data: ~S" event))))) (assert (search expected bytes)) (coerce bytes '(simple-array (unsigned-byte 8) (*)))))) ``` ```console $ mise exec -- tools/lisp.sh examples/control.lisp ``` Prints `CONTROL PASS`, `CONTROL NOTIFICATION PASS` and `CONTROL RECONNECT PASS`. - [`with-reconnection`][api-with-reconnection] reconnects on request and returns fresh observations. It never replays commands. More: [control guide](docs/control.md) · [control README](control/README.md) ## Choose an ASDF system One source distribution, one version, one [changelog](CHANGELOG.md). Load only what you use: | System | Use it for | Additional dependencies | API | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `libtmux` | Captures, CLOS objects and explicit tmux operations | ASDF/UIOP | [Core][api-core] | | [`libtmux/query`](query/README.md) | Native predicates, relations and eager QuerySets | Core | [Query][api-query] | | [`libtmux/regex`](regex/README.md) | CL-PPCRE search and full-match filters | Query, CL-PPCRE | [Query][api-query] | | [`libtmux/json`](json/README.md) | Bounded query document interchange | Query, Jzon | [JSON][api-json] | | [`libtmux/control`](control/README.md) | Queued requests, output streams and reconnection on tmux 3.8+ | Core | [Control][api-control] | | [`libtmux/workspace`](workspace/README.md) | Owned declarations, drift previews and explicit reconciliation | Core, Jzon | [Workspace][api-workspace] | | [`libtmux/workspace/cli`](workspace/cli/README.md) | Workspace validation, previews and explicit-endpoint apply | Workspace | [CLI][api-cli] | Definitions are in [`libtmux.asd`](libtmux.asd); source is in `src/`. ### [`libtmux`](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-lisp/tree/master/src): the core library Captures the CLOS object graph and runs explicit tmux operations through a [`libtmux:client`][api-client], with ASDF and UIOP alone. [API reference][api-cli] · [README](workspace/cli/README.md) ## Support and status - **Unreleased.** Load it from a checkout; the API may change. - **Platform.** SBCL on Linux x86-64, WSL included. [Process requirements](docs/transport.md#supported-process-boundary). - **tmux.** 3.3a or newer. [Control connections](docs/control.md) need 3.8. - **One operation per client.** Calls block; a second concurrent call signals [`client-busy`][api-client-busy]. - **Closing a client leaves tmux running.** [`kill-server`][api-kill-server] is a separate, explicit call. - **Mutations return outcomes.** Read the [`command-outcome`][api-command-outcome] before retrying. [Outcome handling](docs/tutorial.md#handle-command-and-observation-outcomes). - **In development.** Wider event coverage and source filtering. # Capture, inspect and build a workspace

This tutorial builds two sessions, three physical windows, four links and four
panes on a private tmux daemon, then inspects them as ordinary Lisp data. It
touches no other tmux server.

Start with the [source installation](../README.md#install-from-source).

## Run the walkthrough

```console
$ mise run examples
```

The runner:

- creates a private temporary directory and socket, and clears inherited tmux
  variables
- starts an empty-configuration daemon and runs the shipped Lisp examples
- stops its own server
- exits nonzero on any failure

Use another tmux binary:

```console
$ LIBTMUX_TEST_TMUX=/usr/bin/tmux mise run examples
```

## Work at the REPL

Start the REPL from the checkout root. It starts, uses and stops its own
private daemon, so nothing else on the host is touched.

```console
$ mise run repl
```

## Build a linked workspace

The recipe comes from [workspace.lisp](../examples/workspace.lisp). It:

- creates a `logs` window and a `review` session
- splits `editor`
- links the `editor` window into `review` at index 7
- renames `logs` to `logs #{literal}`, keeping the format text literal

Run it once on the fresh demo. A second run fails on the existing names.

<!-- example:workspace -->
```lisp
(defun create-workspace (client)
  "Extend the demo's WORK session; return a fresh captured graph.
Creates a logs window, a second editor pane, a review session and a shared link.
The caller owns the isolated daemon; repeating this recipe there is an error."
  (let* ((before (tm:fetch-snapshot client))
         (work (find "work" (tm:sessions before) :key #'tm:name :test #'string=)))
    (unless work (error "Start the demo's WORK session first"))
    (let* ((editor-link (aref (tm:window-links work) 0))
           (editor (tm:window editor-link))
           (pane (aref (tm:panes editor) 0))
           (logs (observed-value
                  (tm:new-window client work :name "logs" :command '("/bin/cat"))))
           (review (observed-value
                    (tm:new-session client :name "review" :window-name "notes"
                                          :command '("/bin/cat")))))
      (tm:split-pane client pane :direction :horizontal :command '("/bin/cat"))
      (tm:link-window client editor-link review 7)
      (tm:rename-window client logs "logs #{literal}")
      (tm:fetch-snapshot client))))
```
<!-- /example -->

Keep the captured graph after the client closes. The global is REPL scratch,
not a library convention:

```lisp
(defparameter *snapshot*
  (tm:with-client (client :socket-path *socket-path*)
    (create-workspace client)))
```

```lisp
(list (length (tm:sessions *snapshot*))
      (length (tm:windows *snapshot*))
      (length (tm:window-links *snapshot*))
      (length (tm:panes *snapshot*)))
```

The result is `(2 3 4 4)`: sessions, windows, links, panes.

- The two `editor` links differ in session and index, and share one physical
  window.
- `windows` on a snapshot deduplicates physical windows.
- `windows` on a session keeps one entry per link.

All traversal directions: [captured objects](captures.md).

## Select and project locally

<!-- example:selection -->
```lisp
(defun wide-active-panes (snapshot)
  "Select captured active panes at least 40 cells wide; no tmux commands."
  (loop for pane across (tm:panes snapshot)
        when (and (tm:active-p pane) (>= (tm:width pane) 40))
          collect (tm:entity-data pane)))
```
<!-- /example -->

```lisp
(wide-active-panes *snapshot*)
```

This returns a nonempty list of plists from the retained graph. Plain sequence
functions (`map`, `find-if`, `count-if`, `reduce`, `remove-if`) work on it too.
None of these contact tmux.

Compile a reusable scalar filter to validate, inspect or share a selection.
`q` is the package-local nickname for `libtmux.query`.

<!-- example:query -->
```lisp
(defparameter *wide-active-filter*
  (q:compile-filter
   :pane
   '(:and (:= :pane/active t)
          (:>= :pane/width 40))))

(defun wide-active-pane-data (snapshot)
  "Return owned data for captured active panes at least 40 cells wide; no I/O."
  (map 'vector #'tm:entity-data
       (q:matching *wide-active-filter* (tm:panes snapshot))))
```
<!-- /example -->

```lisp
(wide-active-pane-data *snapshot*)
```

- `matching` returns a fresh simple vector in captured order.
- Compilation copies the query form and checks field types, cycles and
  resource limits.
- Neither compilation nor matching contacts tmux. A compiled filter is plain
  Lisp over retained observations.

Traverse relationships locally and keep the eager selection in a QuerySet that
records its root model:

<!-- example:relation -->
```lisp
(defparameter *active-session-filter*
  (q:compile-filter
   :session
   '(:any :session/window-links
     (:is :link/window
      (:any :window/panes
       (:= :pane/active t))))))

(defun active-session-data (snapshot)
  "Return owned data for sessions with an active pane; no I/O."
  (map 'vector #'tm:entity-data
       (q:items
        (q:where (q:from (tm:sessions snapshot) :model :session)
                 *active-session-filter*))))
```
<!-- /example -->

More: [native query guide](queries.md) (quantifier identities, stable
ordering, ownership, strict cardinality).

## Match and serialize an optional query

`libtmux/regex` adds CL-PPCRE operators. Core and `libtmux/query` do not depend
on CL-PPCRE. The scanner compiles once with the filter:

<!-- example:regex -->
```lisp
(defparameter *cat-command-filter*
  (q:compile-filter
   :pane
   '(:regex-full-match :pane/current-command
     (:cl-ppcre "CAT" :case-insensitive-mode t))))

(defun cat-pane-data (snapshot)
  "Return owned data for captured panes whose command is exactly cat; no I/O."
  (map 'vector #'tm:entity-data
       (q:matching *cat-command-filter* (tm:panes snapshot))))
```
<!-- /example -->

```lisp
(cat-pane-data *snapshot*)
```

`libtmux/json` writes the native schema `libtmux.lisp.filter/1`. Reading a regex
filter needs `:allow-regex t`, because parser limits do not interrupt a
CL-PPCRE scan:

<!-- example:filterdocument -->
```lisp
(defun round-trip-filter-document (snapshot)
  "Round-trip the checked regex filter and apply it to one retained snapshot."
  (let* ((document (j:write-filter *cat-command-filter*))
         (restored (j:read-filter document :allow-regex t)))
    (values document
            (map 'vector #'tm:entity-data
                 (q:matching restored (tm:panes snapshot))))))
```
<!-- /example -->

```lisp
(round-trip-filter-document *snapshot*)
```

Both are local. More: [interchange guide](query-interchange.md) (closed
envelope, limits, false/empty/null).

Use both values when false and absence differ. This field is always present,
so an inactive pane returns `nil` and `t`:

```lisp
(let ((pane (find-if-not #'tm:active-p (tm:panes *snapshot*))))
  (multiple-value-bind (value present-p) (tm:field-value pane :pane/active)
    (list value present-p)))
```

- Returned strings, plists and relation vectors are caller-owned copies.
- `entity-data` holds relationship IDs, not a recursive graph.
- Editing a copy never changes tmux.

More: [field reference](fields.md) (types, optional values).

## Handle command and observation outcomes

Creation and named mutations return a
[command-outcome](api.md#command-outcome-type).

- A command can succeed with no observation: its target may vanish afterward.
- Check the observation separately. This helper never retries the mutation:

<!-- example:outcome -->
```lisp
(defun observed-value (outcome)
  "Return an operation's observed value, or signal its observation failure."
  (when (tm:outcome-observation-error outcome)
    (error (tm:outcome-observation-error outcome)))
  (multiple-value-bind (value present-p) (tm:outcome-value outcome)
    (unless present-p
      (error "This operation did not return an observation"))
    value))
```
<!-- /example -->

Rename a captured window and compare the old and new observations:

```lisp
(tm:with-client (client :socket-path *socket-path*)
  (let* ((snapshot (tm:fetch-snapshot client))
         (window (find "editor" (tm:windows snapshot) :key #'tm:name :test #'string=))
         (renamed (observed-value (tm:rename-window client window "api #{literal}"))))
    (list (tm:name window) (tm:name renamed) (tm:same-entity-p window renamed))))
```

The result is `("editor" "api #{literal}" t)`.

- Format punctuation survives literally.
- Refresh uses the **same client context** and returns a new observation.
- Observations from a different connection are not interchangeable targets,
  even when their numeric IDs match.

External failures signal typed conditions. A handler can read:

- [error-outcome](api.md#error-outcome-function)
- [outcome-status](api.md#outcome-status-function)
- [outcome-phase](api.md#outcome-phase-function)
- [outcome-exit-code](api.md#outcome-exit-code-function)
- owned diagnostic bytes

Missing completion evidence can mean the mutation already happened. A blind
retry can duplicate effects. Details:
[operation guide](operations.md#outcomes-and-target-checks).

## Preserve binary data

<!-- example:buffers -->
```lisp
(defun round-trip-bytes (client)
  "Store and retrieve a named binary buffer, including NUL and invalid UTF-8."
  (let ((bytes (make-array 5 :element-type '(unsigned-byte 8)
                           :initial-contents '(0 10 92 195 255))))
    (tm:set-buffer client bytes :name "example bytes")
    (multiple-value-bind (actual outcome)
        (tm:show-buffer client :name "example bytes")
      (assert (eq :succeeded (tm:outcome-status outcome)))
      (assert (equalp bytes actual))
      actual)))
```
<!-- /example -->

```lisp
(tm:with-client (client :socket-path *socket-path*) (round-trip-bytes client))
```

- This returns the five octets unchanged, NUL and invalid UTF-8 included.
- `capture-pane` returns UTF-8 text and an outcome. `capture-pane-bytes`
  returns octets.
- Captures and buffer reads are bounded, complete results, not streams.

Input and pipes:

- A successful send does not prove the application is ready or consumed the
  input. Wait on an application signal, not a sleep or printed text.
- `pipe-pane` sets up a daemon-owned shell pipe. Ownership:
  [pane processes](operations.md#pane-processes).

## Drive an application without polling

The shipped [worker](../examples/worker.sh) signals readiness, reads one
request, writes a receipt file, then signals consumption.

- The Lisp controller waits on a fresh `wait-for` channel per signal.
- The receipt file proves what the application consumed. A successful send or
  printed marker does not.
- Calls block with deadlines. This is not a control-mode subscription API.

<!-- example:worker -->
```lisp
(defun drive-worker (client session socket-path program worker-path receipt-path)
  "Launch a worker through argv, wait for readiness and verify input consumption.
WORKER-PATH names the shipped worker.sh; RECEIPT-PATH is in the owned demo directory.
Signals operational conditions without retrying a mutation. Calls block."
  (let* ((ready (symbol-name (gensym "example-ready-")))
         (consumed (symbol-name (gensym "example-consumed-")))
         (window (observed-value
                  (tm:new-window client session :name "worker"
                                 :command (list "/bin/sh" worker-path program
                                                socket-path ready consumed receipt-path))))
         (pane (aref (tm:panes window) 0))
         (message "release #{literal}; λ"))
    (tm:run-command client (list "-N" "wait-for" ready)
                    :effect :read :timeout 1 :output-limit 4096)
    (tm:send-text client pane message :enter t)
    (tm:run-command client (list "-N" "wait-for" consumed)
                    :effect :read :timeout 1 :output-limit 4096)
    (let ((receipt (uiop:read-file-string receipt-path :external-format :utf-8)))
      (assert (string= message receipt))
      (list :consumed receipt :pane (tm:id pane)))))
```
<!-- /example -->

```lisp
(uiop:with-temporary-file (:pathname receipt :keep nil)
  (tm:with-client (client :socket-path *socket-path*)
    (let ((session (find "work" (tm:fetch-sessions client) :key #'tm:name :test #'string=)))
      (drive-worker client session *socket-path* "tmux"
                    (namestring (truename "examples/worker.sh"))
                    (namestring receipt)))))
```

The result contains `:consumed "release #{literal}; λ"` and a pane ID.

- The request travels as literal text; worker arguments travel through argv.
- The worker stays in its pane until the owned daemon stops.
- Receipt paths are local to the daemon host. This is not a remote-file API.

## Inspect a typed failure

Cancel a read before it acquires data, handle `command-cancelled`, and return
the outcome the condition carries:

<!-- example:condition -->
```lisp
(defun cancelled-read (client)
  "Demonstrate typed failure evidence using a read cancelled before acquisition."
  (let ((token (tm:make-cancellation-token)))
    (tm:cancel token)
    (handler-case
        (progn (tm:fetch-snapshot client :cancel-token token)
               (error "A cancelled read unexpectedly completed"))
      (tm:command-cancelled (condition)
        (let ((outcome (tm:error-outcome condition)))
          (list :condition (type-of condition)
                :status (and outcome (tm:outcome-status outcome))
                :phase (and outcome (tm:outcome-phase outcome))))))))
```
<!-- /example -->

```lisp
(tm:with-client (client :socket-path *socket-path*) (cancelled-read client))
```

The handler never retries. Cancelling a mutation after dispatch can give a
different status or phase. See
[command-cancelled](api.md#command-cancelled-type).

## Stop the daemon

Closing a client leaves its daemon alive. The separate
[`kill-server`](api.md#kill-server-function) operation ends a server. This
helper kills only the explicit socket you pass and accepts success only after
the operation proves both dispatch and daemon exit:

<!-- example:termination -->
```lisp
(defun terminate-owned-server (socket-path &key (program "tmux"))
  "Terminate the explicitly selected owned server and return its proven outcome."
  (tm:with-client (client :program program :socket-path socket-path)
    (let ((outcome (tm:kill-server client)))
      (assert (eq :succeeded (tm:outcome-status outcome)))
      (assert (eq :server-terminated (tm:outcome-phase outcome)))
      outcome)))
```
<!-- /example -->

```lisp
(terminate-owned-server *socket-path*)
```

[`stop-daemon`](api.md#stop-daemon-function) then reaps the daemon you started
and removes its socket directory:

```lisp
(tm:stop-daemon *daemon*)
```

Exit the REPL:

```lisp
(uiop:quit)
```

# Captured objects

`fetch-snapshot` reads the selected daemon and returns a CLOS graph of captured
objects.

- It checks the
  [supported command-alias configuration](operations.md#command-aliases-and-daemon-configuration)
  before listing state.
- `sessions`, `windows`, `panes`, `window-links` and `clients` return fresh
  vectors from that snapshot.
- Those getters, field access, printing, `same-entity-p` and `entity-data` make
  no tmux calls.
- Captured objects stay usable after the client closes.

One-call fetchers:

- `fetch-sessions`, `fetch-windows`, `fetch-panes` and `fetch-clients` capture a
  complete graph and return one vector. Each call reads again.
- Keep one snapshot when several operations must see the same observation.
- Filter a retained vector with ordinary sequence functions, or with
  [`libtmux/query`](queries.md) (validated filters, relation quantifiers, eager
  QuerySets).

## Entities, links and order

- A snapshot holds each physical session, window and pane once.
- A `window-link` records a session, an index and the expected physical window.
- Every link of a window, in the same session or another, is its own
  `window-link`.
- Session-relative active-window state lives on the link.

| Accessor | Captured result |
| --- | --- |
| `sessions snapshot` | Physical sessions in tmux's observed order |
| `windows snapshot`, `panes snapshot` | Physical entities in first-occurrence order |
| `window-links snapshot` | Every contextual link in listing order |
| `window-links session` | That session's links in observed index order |
| `windows session` | One window per link; repeated physical windows remain repeated |
| `panes window` | Physical panes in captured pane order |
| `window-links window` | Every link to that physical window |
| `window pane`, `window link` | The captured physical window |
| `session link`, `session attached-client` | The captured session |
| `clients snapshot`, `clients session` | Attached-client rows, preserving order and multiplicity |

- An attached tmux client is an `attached-client` observation, distinct from the
  library's connection `client`.
- Repeated target names are kept; a name is not an identity.

## Values and ownership

`field-value` returns value and presence as two values.

- Present false: `nil, t`. Absent optional field: `nil, nil`.
- Empty names and pane titles are present strings.
- Current command and path are absent when tmux reports an empty value.
- An empty or zero pane PID is absent. The dead flag keeps the meaning the
  daemon's tmux version reports. Never infer one from the other.

Convenience readers and unknown fields:

- `name`, `active-p`, `width`, `height`, `index`, `current-command`,
  `current-path`, `title` and `dead-p` follow the same presence rules.
- Paths stay text from tmux. They are not normalized as local paths.
- Unknown fields and unloaded relations signal `field-unavailable`.

Fields keep `%`, `$` and non-NUL ASCII control characters exactly:

- The library encodes each field before tmux prints it, avoiding tmux's visual
  escaping (for example an extra backslash before `$HOME` in some releases).
- Literal backslashes and valid Unicode are unchanged.
- The decoder rejects malformed escapes and invalid UTF-8.
- This keeps the text tmux supplies. It cannot recover filesystem bytes tmux
  already turned into display text.
- So a captured current path is not a filesystem identity or a byte-exact
  filesystem argument.

Ownership:

- Every public mutable result is caller-owned: strings, relation vectors,
  provenance and projection containers are copied.
- Entity observations can be shared between result vectors.
- Changing a returned vector or string never changes the capture.
- Mutating private slots is unsupported.

`entity-data` returns a finite plist:

- Holds captured fields, provenance and relationship IDs.
- Omits absent optional fields; keeps present false values.
- Holds no operational handles and no recursive object graph.

`id` gives identity:

- Physical IDs are strings.
- Link IDs are `(session-id index expected-window-id)`.
- Attached-client row IDs mean something only within that observation.

## Identity and refresh

`same-entity-p` compares model, connection context, generation and captured ID.

- Two clients have distinct contexts, even on the same daemon.
- A window link's identity keeps its expected window and index. The index is a
  mutable locator.
- Attached-client identity is scoped to one snapshot.

`refresh` takes the connection client and an entity or snapshot.

- It returns a replacement; the old observation is unchanged.
- A different server generation, a missing target or a changed link mapping
  signals `stale-target`.
- Refreshing an attached client needs a unique live target name and matching
  PID, creation time and tty presence.
- The returned attached client has a new observation identity.

On Linux, a witness detects server replacement even if tmux reuses numeric IDs
and the startup second. It combines:

- daemon PID and startup
- socket inode and device
- process-start identity and a retained pidfd

Daemon and executable versions are recorded separately.

Acquisition:

- Verifies the selected endpoint, then pins later commands to its canonical
  path.
- Tags every listing, even an empty one, with a witness from the same server
  connection as its rows.
- Discards the attempt if the peer changes.
- Ends with continuity checks for server replacement and persistent endpoint
  changes.

It is not transactional: tmux state can change between listing commands.

Tmux launches per capture (client opening and retries excluded):

- Nonempty: five. Alias audit, initial witness, session listing, one batch of
  window-link, pane and client listings, final witness.
- Live empty daemon: four.

The batch:

- gives each listing its own connection witness; both outer witnesses keep the
  full process and socket checks
- has one command outcome. A framing or witness failure keeps it; no
  per-listing outcomes are invented.
- Row limits apply per listing. Stdout and stderr across all launches share one
  byte cap.
- Hooks can change state inside a batch, so graph validation and bounded
  retries stay.

## Bounds and failures

- Provenance holds monotonic and universal-time acquisition bounds, plus tmux's
  Unix server-start time.
- Duplicate physical rows must agree. References, contextual pane order, counts
  and active states are checked.
- Contradictory captures retry at most twice, then signal
  `incomplete-snapshot`.
- Retries share the original deadline and byte budget.

Default limits on fetch operations, with the keyword that sets each:

- total timeout 30 seconds (`:timeout`) and output cap 16 MiB
  (`:output-limit`), inherited from the client
- 100,000 rows per listing (`:row-limit`)
- 100,000 entities per graph (`:entity-limit`)
- 1 MiB per encoded field (`:field-limit`)

`:cancel-token` cancels a fetch. Decoding and graph construction check
cancellation and the same deadline as subprocess work.

- A live daemon with zero sessions returns empty vectors.
- A missing daemon or failed listing signals a condition; it never becomes an
  empty result.
- Acquisition uses tmux's no-start option and never starts a daemon.
- Only entities reachable from sessions are observed. Detached internal tmux
  objects outside that graph are not inventoried.

# Native queries

`libtmux/query` compiles inert keyword-headed data into a reusable Common Lisp
function over captured entities and their registered relationships.

- Compilation and evaluation are local. They never acquire, refresh or mutate
  tmux.
- For a one-off selection that needs no validation or inspection, use an
  ordinary Lisp function.

[Query API](query-api.md) · [Captured fields](fields.md) ·
[Runnable tutorial](tutorial.md#select-and-project-locally)

## Load without global nicknames

Load the separate query system. It loads `libtmux` but no regex, JSON or thread
library:

```lisp
(asdf:load-system "libtmux/query")
```

Applications can choose package-local nicknames:

```lisp
(defpackage #:my-tmux-tool
  (:use #:cl)
  (:local-nicknames (#:tm #:libtmux)
                    (#:q #:libtmux.query)))

(in-package #:my-tmux-tool)
```

The library does not claim the short global package names `tm` or `q`.

## Compile once and match locally

Quoted lists are data. `compile-filter` validates the root model, operator,
field, arity and operand types; it never calls `eval`.

```lisp
(defparameter *editors*
  (q:compile-filter
   :pane
   '(:and
     (:= :pane/active t)
     (:in :pane/current-command ("nvim" "vim"))
     (:>= :pane/width 100))))
```

Use the returned genuine function with standard sequence operations:

```lisp
(remove-if (complement (q:predicate *editors*)) panes)
```

Or request a fresh simple vector with original order and multiplicity:

```lisp
(q:matching *editors* panes)
```

`matching`:

- Accepts a proper finite list or a non-string vector.
- Honors fill pointers and displaced vectors.
- Validates the complete outer container before evaluation.
- Shares one execution budget across the traversal.
- Retains the captured handles; it does not copy the object graph.

## Scalar semantics

| Form | Fields | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `(:= field value)` | Text, integer, Boolean | Typed equality |
| `(:< field n)`, `(:<= field n)`, `(:> field n)`, `(:>= field n)` | Integer | Mathematical integer comparison |
| `(:in field values)` | Text, integer, Boolean | Typed finite membership |
| `(:contains field text)` | Text | Case-sensitive substring search |
| `(:starts-with field text)` | Text | Case-sensitive prefix |
| `(:and ...)`, `(:or ...)`, `(:not expression)` | Expressions | Ordered Boolean composition |
| `(:present field)`, `(:missing field)` | Scalar | Captured presence |

- Text compares by content.
- Integers are Common Lisp integers; wire-decoding bounds do not truncate
  operands. Ratios and floats are invalid.
- Empty AND is true. Empty OR and empty membership are false.
- A bare `nil` filter is invalid.

Presence is separate from truth:

- `(:= :pane/active nil)` compares a present false value.
- A scalar comparison on an absent optional field is false, so NOT of that
  comparison is true. Use `:present` to exclude absence.
- Missing required capture data signals `field-unavailable`.

## Add optional regex operators

Load CL-PPCRE support. Core and `libtmux/query` gain no dependency:

```lisp
(asdf:load-system "libtmux/regex")
```

The operand is owned declarative data: the engine, pattern and closed scanner
options. Search and full match are separate operations:

```lisp
(q:compile-filter
 :pane
 '(:regex-search :pane/current-command
   (:cl-ppcre "^(n?vim)$" :case-insensitive-mode t)))
```

- Boolean options: `:case-insensitive-mode`, `:multi-line-mode`,
  `:single-line-mode` and `:extended-mode`.
- The scanner is compiled once.
- A match at position zero is true. An absent optional text field is false.
- Query visit limits do not interrupt CL-PPCRE scanning. Use regex only with
  trusted local patterns and inputs suited to that engine.

The separate [query interchange guide](query-interchange.md) shows bounded JSON
round trips and the explicit regex read opt-in.

## Traverse captured relationships

Relation forms compile their child expression for the registered target model:

| Form | Relation | Empty or missing behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `(:any relation expression)` | To-many | False on an empty relation |
| `(:all relation expression)` | To-many | True on an empty relation |
| `(:none relation expression)` | To-many | True on an empty relation |
| `(:is relation expression)` | To-one | False when the target is absent |

This expression requires one pane to be both active and running `nvim`:

```lisp
(q:compile-filter
 :session
 '(:any :session/window-links
   (:is :link/window
    (:any :window/panes
     (:and (:= :pane/active t)
           (:= :pane/current-command "nvim"))))))
```

- Two separate `:any` forms may match different panes.
- Missing or unloaded relationship data signals `field-unavailable`. It is not
  a known empty collection.
- `required-relations` reports every traversed relation in first-occurrence
  order.

## Keep eager local selections in a QuerySet

QuerySet is an optional, eager convenience, not a replacement for Common Lisp
sequences. It owns a simple-vector container:

```lisp
(let* ((all (q:from panes :model :pane))
       (editors (q:where all *editors*))
       (wide (q:where-if editors (lambda (pane) (>= (tm:width pane) 120))))
       (ordered (q:order-by wide #'> :key #'tm:width)))
  (q:items ordered))
```

- [`from`](query-api.md#from-function), [`where`](query-api.md#where-function),
  [`where-if`](query-api.md#where-if-function) and
  [`order-by`](query-api.md#order-by-function) return new objects.
  [`items`](query-api.md#items-function) returns a fresh simple vector.
- `order-by` uses `stable-sort` on a private copy, so equal keys keep input
  order. Its predicate and key follow Common Lisp's ordinary sorting callback
  contract.
- `where-if` and `order-by` accept function objects or symbols naming global
  functions. Each designator resolves once before traversal or sorting, so a
  redefinition during a call affects the next operation.
- Macros, special operators and unbound function names signal
  [`invalid-argument`](api.md#invalid-argument-type).
- `where-if` calls its function once per item, in input order, on normal
  completion.
- A declared model is checked against every item. An empty QuerySet can carry
  its model explicitly; `where` can take the model from its compiled filter.
- `one` and `one-or-none` accept QuerySets directly.

## Inspect owned query data

Inspection returns fresh ordinary data:

```lisp
(q:expression *editors*)
```

```lisp
(q:required-fields *editors*)
```

```lisp
(q:explain *editors*)
```

- Changing the source form after compilation, or an inspection result, does
  not alter the compiled filter.
- `fields` returns fresh registry metadata for one of `:session`, `:window`,
  `:pane`, `:window-link` or `:client`. `:client` means a captured attached
  tmux client, not the connection object.
- [`explain`](query-api.md#explain-function) reports `:execution :local` and
  `:source-filtering :unavailable`. Acquisition never executes query filters.
- The [source-execution decision](adr/0001-native-common-lisp-engine.md#qualify-control-mode-and-source-filtering-before-exposing-them)
  records the guarantees still required.

## Select strictly before mutation

`one` requires exactly one item. `one-or-none` returns two values so an empty
selection differs from a singleton containing `nil`:

```lisp
(multiple-value-bind (pane present-p)
    (q:one-or-none (q:matching *editors* panes))
  (when present-p
    (tm:capture-pane client pane)))
```

- Both validate the complete bounded input before returning a candidate, so a
  dependent mutation cannot run before uniqueness is established.
- Zero items signal `no-match` from `one`; multiple positions signal
  `ambiguous-match`.
- Repeated references count as repeated positions.
- The condition says whether its count is exact and exposes a fresh bounded
  sample.

## Resource limits and failures

Default bounds:

- Nesting: 64 containers.
- Compilation: 10,000 structure visits.
- One membership: 1,000 values.
- One string: 65,536 characters.
- Retained query text: 1,048,576 characters.
- Selection: 100,000 items.
- One execution scope: 1,000,000 expression and relation visits.

`compile-filter`, `matching`, QuerySet constructors, `one` and `one-or-none`
take narrower keyword limits for untrusted in-process data.

Failures:

- Cycles, dotted lists, invalid operators, wrong field types and unavailable
  optional systems signal `invalid-filter`. Limit exhaustion signals its
  subtype `query-limit-exceeded`.
- Applying a compiled filter to the wrong captured model or to a plist signals
  `invalid-query-target`.
- Diagnostics keep bounded type and path data. They never print an unbounded
  caller object.

For external configuration files, use the bounded JSON codec. Disabling
`*read-eval*` does not make the Common Lisp reader a query parser.

# Optional query interchange

`libtmux/regex` and `libtmux/json` are separate ASDF systems. Core and
`libtmux/query` need neither. Regex adds CL-PPCRE; JSON adds Jzon.

[Query guide](queries.md) · [Query API](query-api.md) ·
[JSON API](json-api.md) · [Testing](testing.md)

## Load only what the application uses

Enable the two regex operators:

```lisp
(asdf:load-system "libtmux/regex")
```

Enable versioned JSON reading and writing:

```lisp
(asdf:load-system "libtmux/json")
```

Load both before reading a document containing regex nodes. Neither system
contacts tmux.

## Compile a reusable regex

<!-- example:regex -->
```lisp
(defparameter *cat-command-filter*
  (q:compile-filter
   :pane
   '(:regex-full-match :pane/current-command
     (:cl-ppcre "CAT" :case-insensitive-mode t))))

(defun cat-pane-data (snapshot)
  "Return owned data for captured panes whose command is exactly cat; no I/O."
  (map 'vector #'tm:entity-data
       (q:matching *cat-command-filter* (tm:panes snapshot))))
```
<!-- /example -->

- The compiled filter keeps owned pattern and option data plus one prepared
  CL-PPCRE scanner.
- `:regex-search` accepts a match anywhere; `:regex-full-match` requires the
  complete captured string.
- An absent field does not match.
- Parser and query visit limits do not interrupt scanner execution.

## Round-trip a compiled filter

Applications can give `libtmux.json` a package-local nickname such as `j`.
Writing returns a fresh string by default:

<!-- example:filterdocument -->
```lisp
(defun round-trip-filter-document (snapshot)
  "Round-trip the checked regex filter and apply it to one retained snapshot."
  (let* ((document (j:write-filter *cat-command-filter*))
         (restored (j:read-filter document :allow-regex t)))
    (values document
            (map 'vector #'tm:entity-data
                 (q:matching restored (tm:panes snapshot))))))
```
<!-- /example -->

- Without `:allow-regex t`, `read-filter` rejects a regex node before compiling
  its scanner. Non-regex documents need only `libtmux/json`.
- `write-filter` returns a fresh string unless given an open output character
  stream. It never opens pathnames or closes a caller-owned stream.

## Wire envelope

The native schema is `libtmux.lisp.filter/1`:

```json
{"schema":"libtmux.lisp.filter/1","model":"pane","registryVersion":1,"expression":["and",["=","pane/active",false],["in","pane/current-command",[]]]}
```

- The root object is closed and needs exactly the named members.
- Duplicate or unknown members, unknown models, operators or fields, wrong
  arities and unsupported registry versions signal `invalid-filter-document`.
- External names stay strings until allowlist lookup. The decoder never interns
  them.

Operands:

- Boolean false is JSON `false`. An empty membership is `[]`.
- JSON `null` is rejected: registry version 1 has no nullable query operand.
- Numeric operands are integers. Decimal and exponent syntax is rejected before
  Jzon converts the token.
- Native closures and QuerySet callbacks are not serializable.

This schema belongs to the Common Lisp port. Do not assume similar JSON from
another port is compatible.

## Decoder limits

`read-filter` accepts one complete JSON string and defaults to:

| Limit | Default |
| --- | ---: |
| UTF-8 input | 1 MiB |
| Nesting depth | 64 |
| JSON nodes | 10,000 |
| One string | 65,536 characters |
| Membership operands | 1,000 |
| Decimal digits in one numeric token | 128 |

Override a limit with the matching keyword argument.

- An exhausted bound signals `filter-document-limit-exceeded`.
- `document-limit` identifies the bound; `document-path` returns an owned
  location vector.
- Jzon syntax failures and native-query validation failures stay available
  through `error-cause`.

# Explicit operations

Named operations take the connection client first and a captured target where
needed.

- They read current state to validate the target, then use its identity.
- Earlier captures stay unchanged.
- Every operation accepts `:cancel-token`, `:timeout` and `:output-limit`. The
  latter two default to the client settings and cover validation, dispatch and
  any follow-up acquisition together.
- All operations need a live daemon. `new-session` creates a session there.
  Daemon startup is separate; see [managed daemon scopes](daemons.md).
- No operation retries an uncertain mutation.
